title: Table for One: China's Solo Hotpot | China, Explained
description:
A table for one. In China, that's not sad anymore — it's just a way to eat. China's 2020 census counted about 125 million one-person households — roughly one in four homes, up from one in seven a decade earlier. Restaurants adapted, and the clearest sign is the one-person hotpot: your own simmering pot, your own broth, your own pace. Some shops even seat a toy bear across from you. So — a hotpot for one: freedom, or a little bit lonely?

★ Expert Tip: look for the 一人食 ("meal for one") sign or single-seat bar counters — they exist in most big-city malls, and you order a personal pot with no awkwardness.

一人食，在中国早已不是“孤独”，而是一种生活方式。2020 年人口普查显示全国约 1.25 亿个“一人户”，约占四分之一，十年前还只有七分之一。一人小火锅由此流行。你觉得一个人吃火锅，是自由，还是有点孤单？

—
"China, Explained" — one thing about modern China, in under a minute.
🧭 Your China Travel Expert | 你的中国旅游专家
🔊 Narration is AI-generated (OpenAI text-to-speech).

Facts verified 2026-11-21:
• China's 2020 census counted ~125 million one-person households (~25% of all households, up from ~14.5% a decade earlier); solo dining, including the one-person hotpot, is now a major trend: Beijing Review, "Solo living is becoming a common phenomenon in China" (2021) https://www.bjreview.com/China/202104/t20210409_800243041.html + CGTN, "Table for one: Living solo and the culture of quietude booms in China" (2026-01-30) https://news.cgtn.com/news/2026-01-30/Table-for-one-Living-solo-and-the-culture-of-quietude-booms-in-China-1KlBhO14fHG/p.html
